name: Voiceflow
oneLiner: Toronto-based platform for building, testing and running AI chat and voice agents for customer experience, with a visual workflow canvas and LLM-driven playbooks.
bestFor: Restaurant groups with an in-house digital, marketing or CX team that want to build their own custom chat or phone agent (FAQs, reservations, order status) and connect it to their own systems. It is a build-it-yourself platform with no restaurant-specific templates or POS integrations out of the box.

updates.text: Unveiled Voiceflow V4 (generally available to all users by March 2026): agents built from autonomous playbooks, deterministic visual workflows and tools, with the agent routing between them and different LLMs assignable to different parts of an agent.

features: Visual canvas for structured workflows with explicit steps, branches and conditions
Playbooks: LLM-driven skills described in natural language that the agent routes to
Chat agents for websites and messaging, plus voice agents for phone lines
Knowledge base that grounds answers in your own documents and web pages
Choice of AI models per part of the agent (fast model for routing, reasoning model for complex tasks)
API, custom functions and integrations to connect CRMs, helpdesks and other systems
Testing, transcripts and analytics to monitor agent conversations
Shared workspace so multiple editors design and review agents together

pricing.text: Free plan available. Pro about $60 per editor per month and Business about $150 per month, with extra editor seats and usage-based credits; Enterprise is quoted. Figures from third-party pricing reviews; the official pricing page reportedly routes businesses to a demo.

notes: No acquisition or new funding found for 2025-2026 (last round $15M in 2023). Dropped from current review: 'used by over 250,000 teams' (unverified here), 'sub-500ms response latency' (unverified), 'paid plans start from $50/month' (outdated; Pro is now reported at $60), and named Zapier/Make integrations (not confirmed). No restaurant or hospitality customers found; customers listed are general CX brands named on voiceflow.com (Turo and Roam appear on the homepage per search snippets; Vodafone, Sage and Home Depot appear as logos). Credit allowances changed during 2026 (now reportedly dollar-denominated), so re-check pricing before publishing.
